# Wall Street lines up $63 billion for Anthropic's chips

AI labs now pay for their computers through Wall Street. Three banks and Blackstone will fund a company that buys Broadcom chips for Anthropic to rent. Meta enlarged its record share sale. Anthropic aims to list before Thanksgiving, and UBIK gives that a better-than-even chance. Alphabet's weak results set off a global tech selloff.

The AI build also keeps memory scarce, which pushes up Apple's Mac prices. UBIK expects Apple's folding iPhone to stay on sale despite cracked screens. In China, an AI share bubble burst, and UBIK cannot call whether Beijing steps in openly.

The Fed held, and futures and a Reuters poll point to an ECB pause and rises in December. Diesel rose as petrol eased, and UBIK only slightly favours a dip soon.

Congo's Ebola outbreak keeps growing. UBIK sees America keeping its bar on foreigners recently in Uganda.

## Lenders and stock buyers take on AI's chip bill

On Oct. 27, Bank of America, Citi, Morgan Stanley and Blackstone announced $63 billion of financing for chips that Anthropic will use. The money goes to a stand-alone vehicle with one job. The vehicle buys Broadcom's custom AI chips and network equipment and rents them to Anthropic. The three banks arrange about $43.5 billion of senior loans. Blackstone alone supplies the junior debt, about $19.5 billion. Anthropic pays rent, and the rent repays the loans. Deliveries start in 2027.

[Will Anthropic's shares start trading before Thanksgiving?](/forecasts/q_20261027_04)

## Fed and ECB set to hold as diesel climbs

Futures and economists expect the Fed and the ECB to pause this week and to keep a December rise in view. The Fed ends its meeting today, Oct. 28, with a statement at 2 p.m. Eastern. Futures put the chance of no change above 90%. The Fed raised its range to 3.75%–4.00% on Sept. 16, its first rise since 2023. For the Dec. 8–9 meeting, futures priced 73% to 83% for another rise at different times on Oct. 27. The ECB decides on Thursday, Oct. 29. In a Reuters poll, 72 of 73 economists expect it to hold its deposit rate at 2.50%, and 64 expect a rise on Dec. 17. The ECB raised that rate in June and again in September.

[Will Moody's keep France's credit rating where it is on Friday? It settled yes.](/forecasts/q_20261019_04)

[Will diesel cost Americans more in two weeks than now?](/forecasts/q_20261028_01)

## Congo's Ebola cases pass 10,000, mostly outside contact lists

Congo's Ebola outbreak passed 10,000 confirmed cases. Congo's public health institute counted 10,060 cases and 4,887 deaths up to Oct. 25. It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, behind West Africa in 2014 to 2016, and about three times Congo's previous worst. Officials declared it in Ituri on May 15. It now reaches 66 health zones in eight provinces, but Ituri and North Kivu hold nearly all the cases. The pace stays high and flat: about 80 cases a day from August to Oct. 20, and about 71 a day after that.

[Will America keep its Ebola ban on visitors from Uganda?](/forecasts/q_20261028_02)

[Will America keep Nigeria and Kenya off its Ebola travel ban?](/forecasts/q_20261027_03)

## Beijing stays quiet as China's AI stocks fall 40%

China's AI share boom ended in a bust. On Oct. 27 the STAR 50, the index of the 50 biggest companies on Shanghai's tech board, fell 4.81% to its lowest close in 14 months. More than 4,900 mainland shares fell. Reuters put the STAR 50 about 40% below its early-summer peak, with about $480 billion of value gone. The damage spread to the whole market. The CSI 300 blue-chip index entered a bear market, and Bloomberg estimates about $2.4 trillion lost across Chinese stocks since May. The STAR 50 bounced 2.45% on Oct. 28.

[Will Beijing take new steps to prop up stocks by early December?](/forecasts/q_20261028_03)

## Apple raises Mac prices as folding iPhone screens crack

Apple's newest chip reaches ordinary buyers at a higher price. On Oct. 27 Apple put its M6 chip, its first made on a 2-nanometer process, into an entry 14-inch MacBook Pro and a 24-inch iMac. Orders open today, and the machines reach stores on Nov. 6. The MacBook Pro starts at $1,999. That is $300 more than the M5 model it replaces and $400 more than a year ago. Memory costs far more now because AI data centers buy it up, and Apple passes that cost to buyers. TweakTown reports that the base 16GB model gets no faster memory than the M5, below the speed that Apple advertises. Bloomberg reports that Apple will show its first touchscreen MacBook Pro at an event in Los Angeles today.

[Will Apple keep selling the iPhone Duo through Black Friday?](/forecasts/q_20261028_04)

[Will an iPhone Duo ordered on Black Friday still miss Christmas?](/forecasts/q_20261024_03)

forecasts.claim: Will diesel cost Americans more in two weeks than now?
forecasts.resolution_source: US Energy Information Administration, Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update, weekly U.S. on-highway diesel fuel price (all types), https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/
forecasts.resolution_rule: Yes if the US average on-highway diesel price for the week of Nov. 9, 2026, as first published by the EIA, is above $6.352 a gallon, the reading for Oct. 26, 2026 published on Oct. 27. No if it is $6.352 or lower. If the EIA has not published the Nov. 9 reading by Nov. 10, 2026, the question is void.

forecasts.claim: Will America keep its Ebola ban on visitors from Uganda?
forecasts.resolution_source: CDC's order page for the Ebola entry suspension (cdc.gov/port-health/legal-authorities/evdorder.html), the Federal Register, or an official CDC, HHS or DHS statement
forecasts.resolution_rule: The moment that counts is 5:00 pm US Eastern time on Nov. 10, 2026, when the current order expires. Yes if a US federal order in force at that moment bars entry to foreign nationals because they were in Uganda, or any part of it, within a set period before arrival. The order can be a CDC renewal, an amendment, a successor order or a presidential proclamation, issued before or on Nov. 10 or later with effect from that moment, and it counts whether or not Congo and South Sudan are also listed. It must be shown by the source by Nov. 17, 2026. No if no such order is in force at that moment: the order lapsed or ended, or was amended so that having been in Uganda no longer by itself bars a foreign national from entry. Changes after that moment do not alter the answer. Measures that apply only to US citizens or permanent residents, such as routing through designated airports or extra screening, do not count as yes. If by Nov. 17, 2026 the source shows no order in force at that moment, the answer is no.

forecasts.claim: Will Beijing take new steps to prop up stocks by early December?
forecasts.resolution_source: Official announcements on the websites of the State Council, People's Bank of China, China Securities Regulatory Commission, National Financial Regulatory Administration, Ministry of Finance, the Shanghai, Shenzhen or Beijing stock exchanges, Central Huijin or another named state investor; or Reuters or Bloomberg reports of such an official announcement.
forecasts.resolution_rule: Yes if, between 2026-10-28 09:00 UTC and 2026-12-08 23:59 Beijing time, a source body publicly announces a concrete new step to support mainland share prices, as published by it or reported by Reuters or Bloomberg by 2026-12-09 23:59 Beijing time. Counts: (a) Central Huijin or another named state investor says on the record it has bought or will buy mainland shares or stock funds; (b) the central bank creates, enlarges or extends a lending facility for share purchases or buybacks; (c) a cut to stamp duty or other taxes or fees on share trading; (d) looser margin-lending rules, such as a minimum margin deposit below the 100% set in January 2026; (e) a formal slowing or pause of new listings, or new limits on share sales by major shareholders; (f) a rule raising how much insurers or pension funds may or must hold in shares; (g) a new state-backed fund whose stated purpose is buying listed shares. Does not count: general pledges or meeting readouts without a concrete measure; unnamed-source reports of informal guidance; steps announced before the window, including the mid-October guidance, the outbound investment rules effective Dec. 1 and the 60 billion yuan National AI Industry Investment Fund; economy-wide interest-rate or reserve-requirement cuts; companies buying back their own shares; curbs that tighten trading. A step counts once announced, even if later delayed or reversed. Otherwise No.

forecasts.claim: Will Apple keep selling the iPhone Duo through Black Friday?
forecasts.resolution_source: Apple's US online store and Apple Newsroom statements, the US Consumer Product Safety Commission recalls list, and Reuters or Bloomberg reporting on any iPhone Duo sales halt or recall.
forecasts.resolution_rule: Yes if, from the cutoff through the end of Nov. 27, 2026, US Pacific time, Apple neither (a) stops selling the iPhone Duo in the US because of its inner-display or hinge problem, meaning Apple stops taking new US orders for every Duo configuration and Apple, a regulator, Reuters or Bloomberg attributes the pause to the defect, nor (b) announces, or is ordered by a regulator in any country to carry out, a recall of the iPhone Duo, meaning return, repair or replacement offered for units that have not failed. A pause in that window counts even if sales later resume or a revised Duo replaces the original; a pause announced for a date after Nov. 27 does not. These do not count as stopping sales: sold-out notices, long delivery dates, store stock-outs, the current free replacement of failed units, an extended warranty for display failures, or a switch to a revised Duo with no pause in taking orders. Only a halt or recall reported by the end of Nov. 30, 2026 counts; if none is reported by then, the answer is yes.

forecasts.claim: Will Anthropic's shares start trading before Thanksgiving?
forecasts.resolution_source: Nasdaq trading records and Anthropic's pricing announcement or final prospectus (SEC Rule 424(b) filing), as reported by Reuters, Bloomberg, AP or CNBC
forecasts.resolution_rule: Yes if Anthropic's common stock (expected ticker ANT, though a different ticker or share class still counts) begins regular trading on the Nasdaq, or on any other U.S. national securities exchange, on or before Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026 (U.S. Eastern time). The date of the first regular trading session decides; a later halt, delisting or withdrawal does not undo it. Pricing the offering does not count unless regular trading also starts by then. When-issued, pre-IPO, private secondary or tokenized trading does not count. No if regular trading has not begun by the end of Nov. 25, 2026, for any reason, including a postponement or withdrawal of the offering; a postponement still counts as Yes if trading nonetheless begins by Nov. 25. Reports published through Nov. 28, 2026 count toward showing when trading began; if none of the named outlets or Nasdaq records show trading beginning by Nov. 25 by then, the answer is No. The offering's size, price, valuation and first-day performance do not affect resolution.

forecasts.claim: Will America keep Nigeria and Kenya off its Ebola travel ban?
forecasts.resolution_source: CDC Port Health legal authorities page for the order suspending entry from countries where Ebola exists (cdc.gov/port-health/legal-authorities/evdorder.html), the CDC's Oct. 22, 2026 boarding declaration order, and any related Federal Register notices
forecasts.resolution_rule: No if any CDC Ebola order signed from Oct. 27 to Nov. 12, 2026 bars entry to the US, or boarding of a US-bound flight, for presence in Nigeria or Kenya in the prior 21 days. This covers adding either country to the entry suspension order (when renewed, amended or let lapse at its Nov. 10 expiry), to the Oct. 22 boarding declaration order, or to any new or replacement order. It counts even if it takes effect after Nov. 12 or is withdrawn later. Yes otherwise. This includes the case where the CDC page and the Federal Register, as published by Nov. 17, 2026, show no such order. State Department advisory levels, CDC travel health notices, entry limits based on nationality and not tied to Ebola, and screening or airport routing that does not bar entry or boarding do not count.

forecasts.claim: Will an iPhone Duo ordered on Black Friday still miss Christmas?
forecasts.resolution_source: Apple's US online store (apple.com) estimated delivery dates for new iPhone Duo orders, as shown on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. Evidence is a capture of the store page showing those estimates (for example the Internet Archive) or a report by MacRumors, 9to5Mac, AppleInsider or Bloomberg describing them, published by Nov. 30, 2026.
forecasts.resolution_rule: No if, at any time on Nov. 27, 2026 (US Pacific time), Apple's US online store shows an estimated home-delivery date on or before Dec. 25, 2026 for any iPhone Duo configuration (any storage size, colour, unlocked or carrier model). Otherwise Yes if every configuration it offers shows Dec. 26, 2026 or later, or cannot be ordered online (sold out, unavailable or sales halted), including when no configuration can be ordered at all. Where a date range is shown, its earliest date counts; a ship date counts as the delivery date, and a wait such as '4-5 weeks' is counted from Nov. 27. Use the default US estimate shown without a ZIP code, or the estimate for ZIP 10001 if a ZIP is required. Not counted: in-store pickup, walk-in stock, carriers' and other retailers' own channels, and changes to existing orders. A report that gives the store's estimate without naming configurations is read as covering all of them. If no capture or report published by Nov. 30 shows the estimates on Nov. 27, the latest one from Nov. 26 decides, else the earliest from Nov. 28; if there is none from those three days, the answer is No.

forecasts.claim: Will Moody's keep France's credit rating where it is on Friday?
forecasts.resolution_source: Moody's Ratings announcement on France at moodys.com, cross-checked with the Agence France Trésor's France credit ratings page and wire reports (Reuters, AFP).
forecasts.resolution_rule: Yes if Moody's leaves France's long-term issuer rating at Aa3 in every announcement on France published by the end of Oct. 24, 2026 UTC, whatever it does to the outlook or review status, including when it publishes no rating action on France at its scheduled Oct. 23, 2026 review. No if, by the end of Oct. 24, 2026 UTC, Moody's announces any change to that rating, such as a cut to A1 or below, even if the change is later reversed. Void only if, by the end of Oct. 24, 2026 UTC, Moody's formally announces that it has moved the Oct. 23 review past Oct. 24, 2026 and has not changed the rating.

history.why: Moody's test is the December budget, which the riots do not settle by Friday.

forecasts.note: Moody's finished its scheduled Oct. 23 periodic review of France without a formal rating action. The rating stayed at Aa3 and the outlook stayed negative. CNBC, Fortune and Seoul Economic Daily report the same thing. None of the reports found says Moody's changed the rating by the end of Oct. 24 UTC. The time is approximate: Fortune says the announcement came late Friday, and Seoul Economic Daily

evidence.quote: Moody's said it had concluded a periodic review of its rating, leaving it at Aa3, which has carried a negative outlook since last October.
evidence.title: France spared Moody's ratings downgrade as it struggles with unrest

forecasts.reasoning: Moody's ties its negative outlook to whether France's institutions can make policy with a split parliament. The 2027 budget answers that in December, by a vote, by forced passage or by ordinance, and it has not failed yet. Moody's cut France in December 2024 only after a government fell over its budget, and in October 2025 it only turned its outlook negative while S&P cut early. Rating agencies usually count street violence only if it changes the budget or brings down a government. A warning, a negative outlook or a review for downgrade would all leave France at Aa3.
forecasts.uncertainty: The negative outlook is a year old, inside the 12 to 18 months in which Moody's usually settles outlooks. The deficit is now expected near 5.4%, above the 5.0% that Moody's cited in April. The Moody's comment of Oct. 2 was stern, and a cut would only match Fitch and S&P. The riots raised borrowing costs and weakened a minority government that faces the Nov. 5 strike and a no-confidence motion.
forecasts.rises_if: The week passes without new riots, the budget debate moves forward, or France's borrowing costs fall back before Friday.
forecasts.falls_if: New riots break out, a no-confidence motion gains support, the government signals a budget failure, or France's 10-year borrowing cost climbs back toward 5% before Friday.
chain: The Oct. 17 riots added political risk, and France's 10-year borrowing cost rose about 7 basis points on Oct. 19.
Investors read that as raising the odds that Moody's cuts France's Aa3 grade at its review on Friday, Oct. 23.
Moody's said on Oct. 2 that its test is whether France's institutions can still make policy with a split parliament, with the 2027 budget's approval the open question.
That budget is settled in December, and the riots do not decide it by Friday.
Moody's held through the government collapse of October 2025 and cut in December 2024 only after a government fell over its budget.
Will Moody's keep France's credit rating where it is on Friday?

theses.claim: France will get through the riots without losing a credit grade this autumn: Moody's will keep France at Aa3 on Oct. 23 and wait for the 2027 budget's fate in December, and S&P will hold France at A+ at its Nov. 27 review.
theses.missed_link: Coverage treats the riots as one more push toward a downgrade on Friday. But Moody's has named its test: whether France's institutions can pass a budget and make policy with a split parliament. That answer comes in December, and Moody's has acted on France only after a concrete budget failure, holding through the October 2025 government collapse that drove S&P to cut early.
theses.moves: What the French state pays to borrow, and through it home-loan and business-loan rates in France; and the ratings of French banks and state-linked borrowers, which Moody's tends to cut after the state, as it did to several French banks within a week of the December 2024 downgrade.
theses.wrong_if: Moody's cuts France to A1 or lower on Oct. 23, or Moody's cites the unrest as a reason for acting, or Moody's or S&P cuts France before the 2027 budget's fate is settled.
